definitions.explanation: A very polite or honorific way to refer to a person. Used to show respect, especially when referring to someone of high status or someone else's family member.

examples.japanese: あの{御方|おかた}はどなたですか。
{素敵|すてき}な{御方|おかた}ですね。
あちらの{御方|おかた}がお{待|ま}ちになっております。
examples.english: The person over there is waiting for you. (very polite)

notes:
An honorific noun for referring to a person, composed of {御|お} (honorific prefix) and {方|かた} (person, direction). More respectful than {人|ひと} or {方|かた} alone. Often used in formal settings, period dramas, and polite conversation.

POLITENESS LEVELS FOR "PERSON":
- {人|ひと}: person (neutral)
- {方|かた}: person (polite)
- {御方|おかた}: person (very polite/honorific)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- あの{御方|おかた}: that person (respectful)
- {立派|りっぱ}な{御方|おかた}: a fine/distinguished person
- {優|やさ}しい{御方|おかた}: a kind person (spoken with reverence)

USAGE:
More commonly heard in formal or literary contexts. In everyday modern conversation, {方|かた} is sufficient for polite speech. {御方|おかた} appears in historical dramas, formal ceremonies, and when speaking with great deference about someone.

RELATED WORDS:
- {方|かた}: person (polite) — the standard polite form
- {人|ひと}: person — neutral
- お{方|かた}: alternate writing of the same word
- {御仁|ごじん}: person (literary/archaic honorific)
